small_guidance:
- The kernel post-conv is already cheap; runtime (19.4ms vs 5.7ms baseline) is dominated by `nn.ConvTranspose3d`. Tuning BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on the LSE kernel will not close the gap — at most save a tiny fraction of total time.
- If staying small, try BLOCK_SIZE=1024, num_warps=4, and merge the two channel passes into a single online-LSE pass (track running max and rescale running sum) to halve global loads on x.
- Ensure x is in channels-last-3d memory format before the kernel so the C-axis loop reads contiguously, improving the gather pattern over channels.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton kernel — this is the dominant cost. Implement it as a scatter-add of the input × weight outer product into the output grid, handling stride=2/padding=1, with one program per (N, OC tile, output spatial tile). Fuse the LSE+HardSwish+bias+clamp epilogue directly so the (N,16,D,H,W) intermediate is never materialized.
- Better: structure as a gather-style direct conv-transpose where each output element computes its contribution from the relevant input positions; tile across output channels so the LSE reduction over OC happens in registers within the same kernel, eliminating the second pass entirely.
- Use channels-last-3d layout (NDHWC) so the OC reduction axis is contiguous; autotune BLOCK_OC (full 16), BLOCK_SPATIAL (64/128/256), num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}.
